variant: 1 Upper-left shoulder. Preserve the main existing upper-left dune silhouette but widen its near/right shoulder into a gently rising observation patch next to its long curved crest. The one small grooved stone sits at the near end of that shoulder, upper-left of center. Keep middle and bottom clear. No hard-edged plateau.

2 Lower-right shoulder. Keep upper-left dunes and both original rock groups; broaden the lower-right dune's inward-facing shoulder into a comfortable observation spot that rises gently from the center-right sand plain. Place the single small grooved stone at the inner toe of that approach. Dune curves sweep toward bottom right while central crossing remains wide.

3 Upper-center saddle. Extend the nearest upper-left dune gradually toward upper center as one continuous asymmetrical dune with a broad low saddle facing the central plain. The observation spot lies on that saddle, accessible directly from the middle without a drawn road. Single low marker stone rests at one side of the saddle, no stone cluster or cairn. Retain huge open lower half.
